title: Point-contact spectroscopy of electron-phonon interactions and anisotropy of superconducting energy gaps in $2H-NbS{{e}_{2}}$
authors: N. L. Bobrov, L. V. Tiutrina, S. B. Feodos'ev, V. V. Fisun
abstract: The superconducting state of $2H-NbS{{e}_{2}}$ was studied using point contacts for two main orientations of the contact axis relative to the principal crystallographic orientations: along the $c$-axis and in the $ab$ plane. For contacts oriented in the $ab$ plane, dependencies proportional to the electron-phonon interaction function were obtained, which agree perfectly with the theoretical calculation. It was found that the features on the experimental curves associated with the electron-phonon interaction extend to energies twice the cutoff energy of the phonon spectrum and have an amplitude of the same order of magnitude throughout the entire energy range. It has been theoretically demonstrated that the features at energies exceeding the boundaries of the phonon density of states are caused by two-phonon scattering processes of non-equilibrium phonons on Andreev electrons. A criterion for the undisturbed nature of the crystal lattice in the region where gap features form has been found. Using $2H-NbS{{e}_{2}}-Cu$ heterocontacts in the superconducting state, a study of energy gaps was conducted for two orientations of the $NbS{e_2}$ crystal: along the $c$-axis and in the $ab$ plane. It was found that the superconducting energy gaps are anisotropic; specifically, three gaps were identified in the $ab$ plane, whereas only two were observed in the $c$ direction.
summary: This work uses point-contact spectroscopy on 2H-NbSe2 to map out the superconducting energy gap and electron-phonon coupling. The study reveals significant anisotropy in the superconducting gaps when measured along different crystal axes. By analyzing the I-V characteristics and their derivatives, the authors confirm the role of two-phonon scattering and provide quantitative parameters for the superconducting state.
main_problem: The study investigates the electron-phonon interactions (EPI) and the superconducting energy gap anisotropy in the material 2H-NbSe2.
main_result: The superconducting energy gaps are found to be anisotropic, exhibiting three gaps in the ab-plane and only two in the c-direction. Furthermore, two-phonon scattering processes are responsible for features observed at energies exceeding the phonon cutoff.
method: The research employs point-contact spectroscopy to measure current-voltage (I-V) characteristics, analyzing the second derivative for EPI signatures and fitting the overall transport using generalized BTK models.
model_or_system: The physical system is the 2H-NbSe2 superconductor. The analysis uses point contacts oriented along the c-axis and in the ab-plane, requiring theoretical modeling (like BTK theory) to account for multiple superconducting gaps and contact geometry.
key_observables: Second derivative of the I-V curve (for EPI), superconducting energy gaps ($\Delta$), and the anisotropy of these gaps.
important_parameters: Phonon cutoff energy, coherence length, tunneling parameter (Z), and the relative magnitude of the gaps in different crystallographic directions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that inhomogeneous contacts are necessary to isolate the EPI function, and that the BTK model, even when generalized, provides a suitable framework for fitting the multiple gap contributions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the angular dependence of transparency coefficients and show the I-V curve and its second derivative, comparing experimental data against theoretical fits.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the experimental method (point-contact spectroscopy) to probe EPI and gap structure. It then develops theoretical corrections (e.g., for backscattering) and applies generalized superconducting models (BTK) to quantify the observed anisotropy and phonon scattering mechanisms.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of energy gap anisotropy and the role of non-equilibrium phonons provides insights into the pairing mechanism and lattice dynamics in unconventional superconductors, which is relevant to understanding strongly correlated superconducting states.
